differences.detail: The repo's family switch is a substring test on args.net ('llama'/'vicuna'/'mistral'); 'Qwen3-8B' raises ValueError, and only llama/mistral decoder-layer wrappers exist. A Qwen3 path needs a wrapper (or generic layer walker) that builds the DuQuant QuantLinear/QuantMatMul layer for Qwen3DecoderLayer and the matching pairs dict for smoothing.

differences.role: Query/Key states (post-projection, post-RoPE, and post q/k-norm if the model has one)
differences.detail: Repo targets transformers 4.35.2. In 4.51.3 rotary embedding lives on the model and layers receive position_embeddings=(cos,sin); apply_rotary_pos_emb takes no position_ids; layers must accept cache_position/**kwargs; the Catcher must capture position_embeddings (and attention_mask, cache_position) for the calibration inputs; head_dim must come from config.head_dim.

differences.role: Query/Key states (post-projection, post-RoPE, and post q/k-norm if the model has one)
differences.detail: Qwen3 applies per-head RMSNorm q_norm/k_norm (head_dim 128) to q/k after projection and before RoPE. The quantized attention must keep them (fp16, not smoothed or quantized) in that position, then RoPE, then the 128 Hadamard and per-(token,head) quant on Q and K. Select them by name: they are the same Qwen3RMSNorm class as the residual norms, so a class-based smoothing walk must not touch them.

Qwen3-8B is GQA 32/8: v_proj out 1024 != o_proj in 4096, so Lambda_out cannot be folded into v_proj rows. The repo relies on catching a shape exception (quantize/utils.py:192-199) and then divides o_proj's input by Lambda_out online. Detect GQA explicitly from config and implement the online division (and save Lambda_out for reload); do not depend on the exception path.

The repo has no artifact: it evaluates in-process, and --save_dir writes only duquant_parameters.pth (smooth scales, LWC factors, R stacks, permutations), not quantized weights, weight scales/zeros, or the GQA online scale; --resume re-runs duquant() on the fp16 base. The port must save a reloadable artifact (fake-quant weights in the transformed basis + per-layer R/perm/Lambda/online scales + act/QK/V quant settings + config) and an inference adapter that rebuilds the runtime modules: online R1 P R2 on every linear input, per-token asym act quant with lac, the Q/K Hadamard + quant, V quant, the GQA o_proj division. A stock HF load would compute the wrong function.

The repo attention adds an explicit 4-D additive causal mask. In transformers 4.51 with sdpa the model can pass attention_mask=None (relying on is_causal), which the repo's manual attention would treat as no mask (non-causal). Load with attn_implementation='eager' or build the 4-D causal mask (with the cache offset) inside the quantized attention, both in calibration and in the reload adapter.

The run needs act_scales/<net>.pt (per-channel max|x| of every linear input, generate_act_scale_shift.py, 128 x 2048 WikiText2, seed 2) and the rotation table from get_rot.py (needs CUDA). Neither exists in the checkout. The wrapper must generate both for this model (act stats on the fp16 model, before quantization; shifts zero for llama-like) and point main/duquant at them; generate_act_scale_shift.py's model loading/naming must accept Qwen3.

Qwen3 ships bf16; the repo forces fp16. fp16 forward of the fp16 snapshot is fine (WikiText-2 PPL 9.66 measured in the PrefixQuant run), but layer 16 down_proj input has token outliers up to ~2000x the median on token '2'; keep transform/stat computation in fp32 where the repo allows, and watch for inf in act-scale collection and rotation search.
evidence: PrefixQuant run on this model: layer 16 down_proj outlier, fp16 baseline PPL 9.66

differences.detail: The repo's permutation applies x[:, perm] after squeeze(0), correct only for batch size 1. The runtime must permute the last (channel) dimension for any batch/sequence shape (index_select on dim -1).
The repo's greedy rotation differs from paper Algorithm 1 (row index mod block_size swap, signed max-min prefix choice, one random Q' per call). Follow the repo for parity with its reported numbers.
Qwen3 has no linear biases; the zero shift bias buffers the repo adds are harmless (shifts are zero for llama-like). Nothing to rotate or smooth.

Recipe: run.sh (block_size 128, max_rotation_step 256, epochs 0, W4A4, alpha 0.6, smooth, lac 0.9, swc 0.8). --swc overrides LWC, so this is RTN in the transformed basis with no training. block_size 128 divides head_dim (128), hidden (4096) and intermediate (12288).

No packed/int kernel in the repo: the artifact is fake-quant fp16. Weights are per-channel asymmetric and activations per-token asymmetric, so the symmetric shared int8 GEMM kernels (w8a8_int8, prefixquant_w4a4_int8_storage) do not apply as-is; a later kernel stage would need zero-point handling.
Untied embeddings and lm_head stay fp16; DuQuant has no global rotation, so nothing to fold into them.
V is stored fp16 in the cache and quantized per-(token,head) asym 4-bit when read; K is stored after Hadamard + quant. Use the 4.51 Cache.update() API (covered by D2) and keep this order.
evidence: method.md Tensor roles (Value states / KV cache V)

notes: Smoke counts plain nn.Linear modules under model.layers with <= 2^bits unique values per row; the saved/reloaded decoder linears must be nn.Linear (or subclasses) holding the fake-quant weight in the transformed basis (asymmetric per-channel => <= 16 values per row). No library recipes exist for DuQuant.
